slices.focus: Basement cleanup and yard patching make house feel stable; older rescue dog plan moves toward summer target
slices.summary: The house reaches a functional threshold: basement cleanup and yard patching have reduced the constant 'active jobsite' feeling, making daily family life significantly calmer. With this stability, Derek and Erin begin treating the older rescue dog idea as a realistic near-term plan rather than a vague someday dream. They set practical checkpoints — fence testing through weather, a possible weekend dog-sit, and a joint must-have/deal-breaker list — with a summer target if conditions hold. Derek reflects that he cared more about the house feeling stable than checking off every last project.
open_loops: Testing the fence through winter-to-spring weather before committing
Finding a weekend dog-sit opportunity as a household stress test
Writing a joint must-have/deal-breaker list with Erin
Browsing rescue pages as research only (no inquiries until conditions met)
Identifying older-rescue specifics: energy, size, leash manners, alone-tolerance
decisions: By early 2028, Derek and Erin's Brookline row house was mostly functional with only scattered projects left, making dail
